The notation $(f+g)(x)$ means the sum of the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x).$

**Method 1**

To evaluate $(f+g)(4),$ we find $f(4)$ and $g(4),$ and then add the results.

First, we find $f(4)$ and $g(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) & =2(4)+1=9 \\ g(4) & =-3(4)+5=-7\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we add the results:

$$
(f+g)(4)=f(4)+g(4)=9+(-7)=2
$$

**Method 2**

First, we find $(f+g)(x)$ by adding the two functions:

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(x) & =(2x+1)+(-3x+5) \\  & =-x+6 \\  & =6-x\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate $(f+g)(4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}(f+g)(4) & =6-4=2\end{aligned}
$$
